column8: The public label router stores a cloned alias slice under its existing mutex. Caller edits after SetLabelRouting cannot change RouteQuery or RouteWrite, while another explicit setter call remains an authorized configuration change.
NewLabelRouting allocates its own empty label map; no caller container enters the constructor. Later alias handoffs go through the setter that now owns the cloned slice.

CompositeEngine retains an owned alias slice by cloning at this exact setter. No current production routing consumer reads this field; its reserved configuration must still not alias caller storage, and the retention oracle states that limited behavior explicitly.

Before this construction, NewCompositeEngine clones the three caller maps: constituents, backing names and access modes. Intelligent defaults derive from the owned mode map; selected Engine values are retained exactly, so caller map edits cannot replace a bound provider but provider data remains live.

Statement-view issuance clones constituent/name/mode maps and the label-route map while holding the composite read lock. Alias slices are immutable owned entries after SetLabelRouting; later setters replace an entry rather than mutate its slice, so shallow map copying retains a fixed configuration without copying graph data. Nested property routing already clones its maps.

The analyzer setter now clones the handed-over aliases. RouteQuery reads those stored aliases and creates its own result set, so changing the caller slice cannot redirect later queries; an explicit setter can still replace the routing rule.

NewQueryAnalyzer creates three fresh routing/default maps without accepting caller containers. Label configuration only enters through the clone-owning setter; property routes add scalar constituent names into analyzer-owned maps.
